Subject: Follow-up from today — dataplane routing & PII handling

Dylan / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Quick recap from our side and some clarifications we need to keep our security/compliance council comfortable: 

- We need to confirm where tokens and KV cache are stored when a request is pinned to a region (US vs EU). Is KV stored strictly in-region or is there any short-lived replication?
- Retention policy options and whether we can apply per-customer retention windows (90 days / 365 days / custom). Do you provide automated purge/ttl?
- Logging granularity: request vs token-level costs; can we disable storing raw prompts while still keeping metrics/traces?
- Cross-region failover: if US zone is degraded, what route will requests take? Will data flow to APAC/EU or is there a controlled warm-standby behavior?

I attached the high-level data map Emilia shared during the call. We also need an initial estimate of what additional compliance evidence you can provide (SOC2 artifacts, encryption-at-rest key management details).

Next steps for us: legal/security will produce a short questionnaire on Friday — can someone on your side own the answers? Ideally before our Security Review meeting on Dec 22.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Director of Platform Security
Servify Health

Hi Sanjay — great meeting. Short post-call recap and owners below.

Recap (top-line):
- Regional pinning: we support strict region pinning for model execution and KV cache. No active cross-region replication of KV by default — warm-standby is available as an opt-in topology.
- Retention: per-customer retention windows are supported via policy flags (default 30 days); we support custom TTLs and automated purge jobs.
- Logging: we can turn off storing full prompt text and keep structured telemetry / token counts / latency traces.
- Failover behavior: default behavior is region-affinity with controlled failover to a designated secondary region (you choose EU or APAC) — traffic routing is done via smart routing and will only cross borders if your policy allows it.

Owners / next steps:
- Security questionnaire: Monica will own, draft response by Dec 21.
- Evidence: I will pull together a short pack (SOC2 scope, KMS integrations) + our data-handling matrix and share on Dec 17.
- Warm-standby design options and cost delta: Ben will prepare a short one-pager with throughput assumptions and cost (due Dec 18).

Can you confirm: preferred secondary failover region (EU or APAC) and whether Servify requires logs to be retained in-region even after failover? That will change the recommended topology.

Thanks — attaching our initial dataplane notes.

— Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — dataplane routing & PII handling

Sanjay / Dylan — Monica here from Security. A few clarifications and what we can provide for your review: 

1) KV / cache residency:
- By default KV cache and prefix caches are co-located with model execution and do not replicate off-region. We provide an opt-in asynchronous snapshot replication for warm-standby (configurable cadence). Snapshots are encrypted in transit and at rest.

2) Retention options:
- Default retention: 30 days.
- Configurable options: 0 (no retention), 7, 30, 90, 365, or custom (enterprise plan) — TTL enforcement is automatic and irreversible once triggered.
- We can support a per-customer retention policy set at the model endpoint level; enforcement is via our data lifecycle service.

3) Logging and PII controls:
- We support redaction for PII at ingestion (basic pattern redaction + optional custom scrubbing hooks).
- If you opt to disable prompt storage, we retain only telemetry (token counts, error traces, route decisions) and hashed identifiers for correlation.
- Audit logs for admin actions are retained per your requested retention window; logs include redacted request ids, timestamps, and operator ids.

4) Cross-region failover semantics:
- Controlled failover: traffic will only go to the configured secondary region. We do not default to broadcasting traffic to arbitrary regions.
- Data residency during failover: if you require logs and stored artifacts to remain in-region, we can configure synchronous write-through to a customer-managed KMS-backed vault in the original region before allowing failover (this has a latency and cost impact).

Attachments: data-handling-matrix.pdf (pdf, 3 pages)

Ask from us: please confirm whether Servify requires
- synchronous on-region replication for logs/artifacts during failover (yes/no) and
- whether prompt storage is allowed for debug traces (yes/no).

I will start the security questionnaire answers tomorrow and aim to have a complete draft by end-of-day Dec 21 so your Security Review on Dec 22 has something to hand.

— Monica Patel
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Emilia Rogers <emilia@servifyhealth.com>

Thanks Monica — two quick answers from our Security Council that will help your draft: 

1) We want logs/audit artifacts to remain in-region unless we explicitly approve a failover (so synchronous write-through for critical artifacts preferred).
2) Prompt storage: we would like an option that keeps prompts off by default; for debug windows we can enable short-lived prompt capture (7 days) under an NDA.

We'll confirm formally in the questionnaire but wanted to give you a heads-up. Also requested that Ben's cost delta packet include both a warm-standby snapshot option (asynchronous) and a synchronous write-through option so we can compare.

Thanks — Emilia
